title: Pesto Chicken Pizza
subtitle: Basil pesto, sun-dried tomato, chicken
description: Basil pesto, sun-dried tomato, chicken. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Season chicken and prep toppings
steps.instruction: Slice cooked chicken and season lightly with salt. Halve cherry tomatoes and toast pine nuts in a dry skillet until golden — watch them; pine nuts go from toast to trash in seconds.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 500°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 500°F at least 40 minutes. Pesto burns if the stone is not fully saturated.

steps.title: Stretch and pesto base
steps.instruction: Stretch dough to 12–14 inches. Spread pesto in a thin even layer — thick pesto globs stay raw-tasting in the center. Leave a clean rim for blistering.

steps.title: Mozzarella, chicken, tomatoes
steps.instruction: Layer fresh mozzarella, chicken, and cherry tomatoes cut-side up so they roast. Sprinkle parmesan. No tomato sauce on pesto night.

steps.title: Bake until pesto edges darken
steps.instruction: Bake 10–13 minutes until cheese melts and pesto oil sizzles at the edges. Tomatoes should wrinkle slightly. Rotate once.

steps.title: Pine nuts, balsamic, and cut
steps.instruction: Scatter pine nuts and drizzle balsamic glaze after the bake. Rest 2 minutes, cut 8 slices. Pesto Chicken Pizza — green sauce, bright finish, hall-approved.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Pesto Chicken Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Basil pesto, sun-dried tomato, chicken. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free pizza crust.
